monument_name: Bistabara Śikhara Temple 1 (built around the 13th-15th cent.)
description_en: Bistabara Śikhara Temple 1 is one of threeśikharatemples built in a row (around the 13th-15th centuries) beneath the village of Bistabara. The Bistabara village committee has built a stone and cement wall around the monuments. Temple 1 is the easternmost monument of the complex. It has a north-west orientation. The door faces the central and tallestśikhara(JUM0451) of the complex, and the pediment is ornamented with carved horizontal friezes. The doorjambs are also decorated with spirals. A flower or star pattern is in the centre of the door lintel. The ceiling is also embellished with a flower or star pattern and the sanctum, which may have originally housed aśivaliṅga, is now empty. Theśikharais crowned by twoāmalakadiscs.Locals refer to the Bistabaraśikharatemples as Pañcadevala, which translates as "five temples." This prompted D. R. Sharma to speculate that the site once housed five temples (Sharma 2012: 181-182). This is highly unlikely, because "Pañcadevala" is a term commonly used in west Nepal to refer to locations with more than oneśikharatemple. Furthermore, the Pañcadevala plan is mostly found in the districts of Dailekh, Achham, and Kalikot, which correspond to the Rāskoṭi kings' domain. This dynasty ruled from the late 14th century to the late 18th century (Andolfatto 2022). So far, no Pañcadevala has been discovered in the Jumla district.From the 13th to the 15th centuries, suchśikharatemples were built throughout the Karnali Basin (Andolfatto 2019). Rarity of inscriptions onśikharatemples (locally known asdevala) complicates dating of these monuments. The pediments of the Bistabaraśikharatemples have horizontal friezes that are identical to those found on Tarpibada's twośikharatemples (JUM0441andJUM0442), 2.5 kilometres to the north. These temples were built between the 13th and 15th centuries. A stone memorial pillar located 5 metres north of the Bistabara temples (JUM0453) also bears the date ŚS 1422 (1500 CE). It's possible that the pillar and the temples were constructed at the same time.
monument_assessment: Restored, Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
